concern.concern: Proof 5.1 concludes that each field evaluation is measurable with respect to the completion of G=σ(Y(e_n):n), and hence that the full field sigma-algebra is contained in that completion. Almost-sure equality with a G-measurable variable only gives this for the ambient augmentation by all ambient null events; it need not give membership in the ordinary completion of G. For example, take X=H=R, K=0, ε=1, an independent standard-normal prior U, standard-normal ξ and an independent Bernoulli(0) coordinate with event N={coordinate=1}. Set Z(g)=gξ except Z(2)=2ξ+1_N. This satisfies the stated Gaussian and L2-linearity assumptions. With supplied basis {1}, G=σ(ξ), while the full field reveals N through Y(2)−2Y(1). N is not contained in any G-measurable null set. The theorem's independence conclusion remains accessible directly from the already established independence with every finite observation block and a generating-cylinder argument, but the written completion inclusion needs qualification.

original_concerns.reason: The ordinary completion assertion fails for the stated L2-equivalence-class noise interface. On R×R×{0,1} with product normal, normal and Bernoulli(0) laws, N={last coordinate=1} is ambient measurable and null but has no sigma(xi)-measurable null superset. Changing only Z(2) by 1_N preserves all finite Gaussian laws, L2-linearity and independence from U. Yet Y(2)-2Y(1) reveals N. Thus the claimed inclusion in the ordinary completion is false. The already proved independence of every finite residual-coordinate block and every finite arbitrary observation block extends twice by the existing measure-uniqueness supplier, directly to the full cylinder-generated field sigma-algebra. No theorem hypothesis, posterior formula, all-data kernel branch or supplier changes are needed.

required_own_edits.source_excerpt: Finite basis-coordinate cylinder rectangles have the product of their marginal probabilities; since they form a generating pi-system for the joint Borel and basis-observation sigma-algebras, [F9] extends this identity and proves that $W$ is independent of $\mathcal G:=\sigma(Y(e_n):n)$. To compare with the full field sigma-algebra, write the supplied basis of $H$ as $e_1,\ldots,e_m$ if finite, allowing $m=0$, or as $(e_n)_{n\ge1}$ if countably infinite. For finite $m$ put $P_Ng=\sum_{1\le n\le\min(N,m)}\langle g,e_n\rangle_He_n$; for an infinite basis put $P_Ng=\sum_{1\le n\le N}\langle g,e_n\rangle_He_n$. In either case the empty sum is zero, $r_N:=g-P_Ng$ tends to zero, and in the finite or empty case $r_N=0$ after the basis is exhausted. The mean-square error of $D_N:=Y(g)-Y(P_Ng)$ is at most $(\|Km_0\|^2+\|K\|^2\|C_0\|+\epsilon^2)\|r_N\|^2$. Choose the least $N_k\ge k$ with $\|r_{N_k}\|\le2^{-k}$. For each positive integer $r$, Markov gives $\mathbb P(|D_{N_k}|\ge1/r)\le r^2(\|Km_0\|^2+\|K\|^2\|C_0\|+\epsilon^2)4^{-k}$, a summable bound; [F11] implies $|D_{N_k}|<1/r$ eventually almost surely. The countable intersection over $r$ still has probability one, so $D_{N_k}\to0$ and each field evaluation is measurable with respect to the completion $\overline{\mathcal G}^{\mathbb P}$. Thus $\sigma(Y(g):g\in H)\subseteq\overline{\mathcal G}^{\mathbb P}$. Independence of $W$ from $\mathcal G$ extends to its completion because every completed event differs by a null set from an event in $\mathcal G$; therefore $W$ is independent of the full field. [given, F3, F6, F7, F9, F11, F12, step 3.1, step 4.1, choose, construct, algebra]
required_own_edits.proposed_replacement: For a fixed finite list of observations, finite basis-coordinate cylinder rectangles and observation rectangles have the product of their marginal probabilities by the independence just proved. These rectangles form a generating pi-system for the product of the residual Borel sigma-algebra and the finite observation Borel sigma-algebra, so [F9] extends the product identity and shows that $W$ is independent of this finite observation block. Now fix any $A\in\mathcal B(X)$. The finite measures $C\mapsto\mathbb P(W\in A,C)$ and $C\mapsto\mathbb P(W\in A)\mathbb P(C)$ agree on the pi-system of finite observation cylinder events, including the whole space. By [F9] they agree on $\sigma(Y(g):g\in H)$. Since this holds for every $A$, $W$ is independent of the full field. This argument includes finite and empty supplied bases and requires no inclusion in the ordinary completion of a basis-observation sigma-algebra. [given, F3, F6, F7, F9, F12, step 3.1, step 4.1, construct, algebra]
